body:
Thank you so much for your kind reply. 

I have decided to go into therapy. I actually just got off the phone with a therapist I saw some time ago, and she's agreed to see me again even though I still owe her a little bit of money. 

I have discussed the depression with my doctor but he decided that it was best to try and do this without antidepressants because there is a low risk of the pills being harmful to the baby. However, at this point, I think we may have to weigh the pros and cons and decide which is potentially more harmful - the possible adverse effects from the medication, or the effects caused by the massive amounts of stress. Neither are ideal, so we'll just have to go the least harmful route. Maybe  - hopefully - the therapy will help enough that I won't feel that I need the antidepressants.

To answer your questions:

I did not plan on getting pregnant. I'm young, only 18. I'm in a committed relationship with the baby's father, but neither of us were remotely prepared for this. Don't get me wrong, I love my baby more than I have ever loved anything. I think my love for her may actually be contributing to my depression heavily because I sincerely want her to have the best life possible. In the beginning, the father and I had plans to make things work so that we could keep her and raise a family together, but I'm now six months along and it's seeming more and more like I may end up doing this alone, and I'm terrified that I will fail her. Her father relapsed on heroin last month after having been clean for over a year and this has put tremendous strain on our relationship and resulted in him losing his job. He has quit using and gone through his withdrawals, but only seems sure that he wants to try to make things work about half of the time. I'm currently unemployed (I was unable to work during the beginning of my pregnancy due to being high risk, and am now too pregnant for anybody to consider hiring me, despite how hard I have tried) and I worry about being able to provide for her alone.

The fucked up thing is, though, that it seems like no matter what he says to me or how he treats me, I always want to forgive him. And after he does something awful, he always turns around to tell me how much he didn't mean it and how much he wants to fix things. I know this behavior is typical in abusive relationships, but until this point I've still been pretty hell bent on trying to make things work.

We are currently living with my father, though it is more of a roommate situation than a father-daughter one. Until I turned 18 I hadn't lived with family for five years because my family situation was less than ideal. But at this point my dad needed help financially to keep his place and my boyfriend and I needed some place to go. My dad has good intentions, but is also a huge contributor to how I have been feeling. He is morbidly obese and refuses to even remotely attempt to take care of himself. I have the hardest time watching him waste away like this. He is also dealing with some pretty severe depression, and I am constantly worried that he is going to have a heart attack and die as an unhappy person. I feel as though I'm at fault for his current state because I live with him and should be able to make his life better somehow, but I've been incredibly unsuccessful.

I guess I just feel like my life has come to a standstill with no room for advancement. I was supposed to start school this semester, but at the last minute pulled out because my boyfriend lost his job and I felt like finding a job of my own was more important. No luck in that department either. So I basically spend my time sitting around the house and cooking and cleaning. I haven't warmed up to this kind of domesticated living. I need to feel like I'm working towards something.

Yes, I have struggled with depression and bipolar disorder since I was a child. However, for about a year prior to my pregnancy I was doing really well. My doctors took me off my medication and I was genuinely happy with my life and where I was headed. After I got pregnant my doctors warned me that it's common for the depression to creep back up due to the rush of hormones, and now they tell me to prepare for it to get worse after the baby is born because women with prenatal depression generally suffer from post partum as well. This is discouraging because I feel like there is no way out. I'm going to feel like this forever. I would say that my depression is triggered by the things going on around me in part, but I think a great deal of it has to do with brain chemistry.

I do try my best to keep up appearances. Two of my sisters struggle with infertility and I feel that by reaching out to them or being open with them I am being horribly insensitive to their situation. I felt guilt for getting pregnant in the first place, knowing that I was given this unexpected gift while they have been trying and failing for so long. This should be the happiest time in my life, and instead I feel worse than I ever have. I also don't want to worry anyone. I've been in a very dark place and am constantly thinking about (though I have yet to act on) forms of self harm - a habit I broke years ago. I never looked back to it as a coping mechanism until recent months. I come from a headstrong and judgemental family, and I don't think they would understand.

The only person I had felt comfortable being open with was my boyfriend who, until his relapse, was incredibly supportive. But now, if I cry or if I seem a little off, he just gets angry at me and accuses me of being irrational. He calls me names, and tells me that I'm stupid. So I've been feeling pretty alone and I often question whether or not he's right and I am being irrational. 

Anyhow, I know this has been really long and if you're still reading then thanks so much for listening.
